Retry a function when it fails

Source: R/retry.R
retry.Rd

Decorator that calls a function again until it succeeds or a stop condition is met, sleeping between attempts. Port of Python's tenacity.

Usage

retry(
  f,
  stop = stop_never(),
  wait = wait_none(),
  retry = retry_all(),
  before_sleep = before_sleep_none(),
  after_sleep = after_sleep_none(),
  reraise = FALSE,
  retry_error_callback = NULL
)

Arguments

f

The function to decorate. Usually supplied by %@% rather than directly.

stop

A stop condition, e.g. stop_after_attempt(). Defaults to never stopping.

wait

A wait strategy. Defaults to no waiting.

retry

A retry condition. Defaults to retrying every error.

before_sleep, after_sleep

Hooks run before and after each sleep, see before_sleep_log() and after_sleep_log().

reraise

If TRUE, re-throw the last error when stop fires instead of throwing a fnware_retry_error.

retry_error_callback

Optional function called with the final state when stop fires. Its return value is returned instead of throwing. The state is a list with attempt, wait, elapsed, error and value.

Value

A decorator. The decorated function returns the first acceptable result, or signals a fnware_retry_error condition (with $attempt, $error and $value) once stop fires.

Details

Call retry(stop, wait, retry, before_sleep, after_sleep, reraise, retry_error_callback) to build a decorator, then apply it with %@% or by calling it on a function.

Examples

n <- 0
flaky <- function() {
  n <<- n + 1
  if (n < 3) stop("not yet")
  n
}
retry(stop = stop_after_attempt(5))(flaky)()
#> [1] 3

# Back off exponentially between attempts
f := retry(stop = stop_after_attempt(3), wait = wait_exp(min = 0.1)) %@% function() 1
f()
#> [1] 1
